Judgment

(PER : AMIT B. BORKAR, J.) :
-
1.

In this application, the applicant has prayed that the First Information Reports registered for the offence punishable under Sections 188, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) read with Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the Act of 2006") be quashed.

The main thrust of challenge is that the allegation in the FIR does not spell out offence under the provisions of the Act of 2006 and Rules framed under it and consequently offence 2 cr-apl-489-14j.odt under section of the IPC is not made out.

sentences.text: 2. This Court on 04.08.2014 issued notices to the non- applicants and by way of ad-interim order it was directed that the investigation may proceed but, charge-sheets under Section 328 of the IPC may not be filed.
By order dated 31.10.2014, the present application along with connected matters was admitted and interim order granted earlier was confirmed.

3. The non-applicant no. 1 has filed reply and submitted that registration of the FIR under Section 328 of the IPC cannot be faulted, as the material on record fulfills ingredients of Section 328 of the IPC.

Shri T. A. Mirza, learned A.P.P. invited our attention to the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Sayyed Hassan Sayyed Subhan and ors. [2018 AIR (SC) 5348] and submitted that it is open for the Food Safety Officer to independently filed complaint before the Competent Court for the offence under provision of the Act of 2006.

The learned A.P.P.
further submitted that the investigation in all the matters is completed and charge-sheets are ready.

He also invited attention of this Court to the order passed by the Division Bench of this Court in LD-VC-CRI-APPLICATION (APPA) No. 452/2020 in the case of Ritesh Rajkumar Toshniwal Vs.
State of Maharashtra (one of us Justice Z. A. Haq is a party) and submitted that 3 cr-apl-489-14j.odt similar order to be passed in the present applications as as facts of present of application are similar.
4.

sentences.text: Today when the matter was called out, the Advocate for the applicant was absent.

Since the facts in present matter are similar to the batch of Criminal Application no. 444 of 2014 and others, which were on board today tagged along with present application, which we have disposed of today by common judgment, we disposing of the present application in terms of the similar order by which we have disposed of the batch of the applications today.
5 . W e a r e o f t h e v i e w t h a t i n v i e w o f t h e j u d g m e n t o f t h e D i v i s i o n B e n c h i n LD-VC-CRI-APPLICATION (APPA) No. 452/2020, we need to pass the similar order.
In the present matters also, the investigation is complete and charge-sheet is ready.
Therefore, considering the aforesaid facts, we are not delving into the merits of the matter at this stage.

In our view, interest of justice would sub- served by passing following order :-
(i) The Investigating Agency shall file charge-sheet within one month from today.
(ii) The Food Safety Officer will be at liberty to file complaint under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

4 cr-apl-489-14j.odt (iii) As we have not delved into the issues raised by the applicant, it will be open to the applicant to avail appropriate remedy for redressal of his grievance, as per law, after filing of the charge- sheet.
The Criminal Applications is disposed in the above terms.
